transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-08-26 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Sarah Nguyen (Redwood AE), Tom Ellis (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (NovaHealth Head of ML), Aaron Cole (Product), Diego Ruiz (Eng Manager)
Shared artifacts: https://redwood.app/pilots/CRM-54912/pilot-results-sheet.xlsx, security-pack.pdf, prompt-set-v2.docx

[00:00] Sarah: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this to 45 minutes. Quick roll call - Tom, Maya, Aaron, Diego here?
[00:08] Tom: Yep, here.
[00:10] Maya: Here.
[00:12] Aaron: Here.
[00:14] Diego: Here.
[00:18] Sarah: Cool. The agenda: quick recap, results from the last run, regression checks after prompt changes, guardrails discussion, and actions. Tom, you wanna kick off with the numbers?
[00:28] Tom: Sure. So we re-ran the eval with the new prompt set v2 that Maya sent last week. I ran a 5k sample across the two main intents: triage and eligibility. Baseline intent accuracy on the hosted model before tuning was about 0.84, after prompt tuning we saw 0.879 overall, so roughly +3.9 percentage points.
[00:50] Maya: That seems right, though our rubric weights false positives higher, so your aggregate number looks better than our weighted score. We got a weighted score of 0.86 because some FP cases are costly for us.
[01:03] Tom: Yeah I noticed that - the internal scoring used exact-match on intent and a loose hallucination heuristic, whereas you guys penalize some hallucinations that reference medical guidance more strongly.
[01:16] Aaron: Quick question - when you say hallucination heuristic, is that automated or manual review?
[01:21] Tom: A mix. We have an automated detector that flags hallucination-like tokens, then we spot-check. For the POC we did a 200-sample manual spot-check and found the detector undercounts certain PHI-sensitive hallucinations.
[01:36] Maya: Right, that's the issue - a lot of the false positives are actually model confident but wrong medical advice.
[01:42] Diego: Are those concentrated on long-form answers or the short clarifying ones?
[01:47] Tom: Mostly the long-form; when the model generates follow-up steps it sometimes invents lab values or suggests tests that are out of scope.
[01:55] Sarah: Ok, so regression check: any deterioration vs last week?
[01:59] Tom: We compared last week's run to this week's with same eval set. There is a small regression on hallucination detection - false-positive rate up ~4% in the automated metric, probably because prompt changes increased verbosity. But intent accuracy improved.
[02:16] Maya: So trade-off: better intent, slightly worse hallucination. We can accept a small drop if we tighten guardrails.
[02:24] Aaron: What's the latency impact of the new prompts? We care about p95 latency while keeping throughput.
[02:29] Tom: On Hosted endpoints p95 increased from 420ms to 470ms average for the standard sequence length. Not huge, but if you go to Dedicated with optimized kernels and batching we can bring that down to ~320-350ms p95.
[02:45] Diego: Are those numbers for the quantized variants? We're running int8 on our infra for cost reasons.
[02:51] Tom: These are for the float16 baseline on Redwood hosted. Quantized variants drop token throughput some times; on xformer quantization we saw ~10-15% lower token cost but latency was similar - depends on sequence length.
[03:05] Maya: Back to quality - what about regression on edge-case prompts? We had two failure modes last cycle: PII leakage and advice outside scope.
[03:14] Tom: Good point. We re-ran the PII set (n=300). PII leakage was essentially zero in automatic tests, but manual review found two instances where the model included an example that could be considered identifying. Probably prompt needs an explicit "never reveal patient identifiers" guardrail.
[03:31] Sarah: We'll add that to the guardrail repo. Tom, can you add the explicit guardrail template?
[03:35] Tom: Yep, will add.
[03:36] Maya: Also for the medical advice, can we have a safety fallback that triggers "I don't have the authority to provide medical advice" and route to a templated response?
[03:44] Tom: Yes, Redwood supports response-level routing; we can add a policy that if hallucination detector score > threshold, return canned fallback or escalation. There's an example in the security pack I linked.
[03:55] Aaron: How often does that detector misfire? We don't want too many false negatives or false positives that degrade UX.
[04:01] Tom: Right now it's tuned conservatively to avoid false positives, but we can push threshold tighter for NovaHealth. That will increase fallbacks but reduce risky outputs.
[04:12] Diego: For the pilot, we need to log those fallbacks for audit. Is that captured in the console?
[04:18] Sarah: Yes, the Redwood Console has per-route tracing and we can tag responses with policy hits. Logs can be delivered to your S3 or a secure bucket; we also support KMS-managed encryption.
[04:29] Maya: Speaking of encryption, status on SOC2 + KMS? Diego and I reviewed the pack, but can you confirm key rotation and audit log retention?
[04:39] Tom: SOC2 in progress for some regions; we provide KMS integration for private deployments and Dedicated. For hosted, we support customer-managed keys via KMS for the private plane options. Rotation is configurable; audit logs can be retained per contract. I'll include specifics in a follow-up doc.
[04:55] Maya: Great. Back to the eval - Tom you mentioned a 5k sample; can you break down per-intent numbers?
[05:03] Tom: Sure. Triage intent (3k samples) accuracy 0.885 after tuning; eligibility intent (2k) 0.868. Hallucination rate overall 0.07 flagged by detector, manual review suggests true hallucination ~0.09 on the weighted set.
[05:20] Aaron: Those are pretty good. For our acceptance criteria we had intent >=0.88 and hallucination <=0.05 weighted. So we're close on intent, off on hallucination.
[05:30] Maya: That means more prompt tuning and guardrail tightening. Tom, can you try prompt compression - shorter system instruct plus few-shot examples - to reduce verbosity that seems to cause hallucinations?
[05:42] Tom: Yep, that's on the list. I tried a compressed prompt in a quick run and saw hallucination down ~1.5 points, but intent dropped a bit. I'll run an ablation and share the spreadsheet.
[05:54] Sarah: Also on the infrastructure side - if NovaHealth opts for Dedicated we can run model variants with different quantization and kernel selection to hit latency/cost targets. Diego, any initial preference?
[06:05] Diego: We'd like to see an apples-to-apples comparison: latency, cost per 1k tokens, and expected p95 under load. Can you include estimated cost for 200k tokens/day?
[06:16] Sarah: Yes, we'll include that in the pricing sheet. Tom, please add performance delta for quantized vs full precision.
[06:22] Tom: Will do.
[06:23] Aaron: On acceptance criteria - if we hit intent >=0.88 and hallucination <=0.06 we'll be comfortable moving to a short Dedicated pilot.
[06:33] Maya: Agree. Also need exact phrasing for guardrails so legal can sign off.
[06:38] Sarah: We'll add a guardrail appendix to the security pack and share a version that legal can comment on.
[06:44] Tom: A note on regressions: the small hallucination uptick coincides with one of the system prompt edits that added proactive clarifying questions. That change reduces under-generalization but increases creative completion. We'll try an alternate phrasing that asks for "do not invent facts; if unsure say I don't know" which tends to reduce hallucination.
[07:05] Maya: Please include the exact text candidates in the doc so we can pick.
[07:09] Tom: Ok.
[07:11] Sarah: Any blockers from your side on going to the next step?
[07:15] Diego: We need access to test logs and to confirm ingestion of our sample dataset. Also want to run a small security scan on the Dedicated image if we go that route.
[07:24] Sarah: We'll provision test access to the staging endpoint and upload instructions to the shared drive. For Dedicated images we can share the container checksum for your security team and schedule a scan window.
[07:35] Aaron: Good. Timing - we're targeting a decision on pilot mode (hosted vs dedicated) by early September.
[07:41] Sarah: Sounds good. Tom, summary of technical tasks?
[07:45] Tom: Re-run 2k evals with compressed prompts and updated guardrail triggers, add explicit PII/PHI never-reveal line to system prompt, tune hallucination detector threshold for lower false negatives, share spreadsheet.
[07:58] Maya: And we'll update the weighted scoring rubric and mark which failures are showstoppers.
[08:04] Sarah: Great. Any final questions?
[08:07] Diego: One small ask - can we get an example of the canned fallback text so design can review UX?
[08:13] Tom: Yep, I'll include three variants - soft refusal, redirect to resources, and escalation to human.
[08:19] Sarah: Perfect. We'll follow up with the artifacts and action items. Thanks everyone.
[08:24] Maya: Thanks.
[08:26] Aaron: Thanks all.
[08:28] Diego: Thanks.
[08:30] Sarah: End meeting.

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-hears (e.g., "Redwood Dedicate" instead of "Dedicated" in automated caption), filler words, and speaker overlap. Attachments: pilot-results-sheet.xlsx (latest evals), prompt-set-v2.docx, security-pack.pdf.
